I need to carefully examine all the bugs.

The first bug is a mention lookup limit. Members with the longest tenure are excluded from mentions in large workspaces, so they get no alerts. Recent members still work. The `MENTION_LOOKUP_LIMIT` of 100 likely causes this.

The member list is ordered newest first, so the oldest members sit beyond the 100-item scan limit. Handle highlighting still works because it relies on regex matching alone, but mention resolution fails for anyone outside that window.

The lookup must scan all members, not just the first 100. A second bug is that `byHandle` uses a Map, so when multiple members share a handle, only the last one gets stored and the rest are lost.

The expected behavior is stricter than the current code. Mentions must be resolved purely from the comment text, excluding the author and any mentions inside code spans. Only active members of the current workspace should be considered, and members from other workspaces must never be included. The current implementation incorrectly merges client-provided IDs with server-resolved ones, which violates the requirement to match exactly what the text says.

Read-only members are skipped during mention resolution. The code explicitly excludes viewers, but the expected behavior requires all roles to be mentionable.

Viewer alerts are not blocked by notification preferences. Each recipient's own settings apply as for any other alert.

A third bug causes duplicate alerts. When an assignee is also @-mentioned on a comment, the system sends both a comment-created notification to watchers and a separate comment-mention notification to that same user.

The expected behavior requires each person to receive at most one alert per comment, and a mention alert must take precedence over a comment alert.

A fourth bug is that replies never notify the parent comment author. The fix is to include the parent author in the watchers list, but only send them a mention alert if they are also explicitly mentioned.

Nested replies are missing from issue threads. The thread list only fetches direct replies, so replies to replies are stored but never displayed under their parent comment. The expected behavior requires every reply in the chain to appear under its top-level ancestor, ordered by posting time.

A fifth bug causes replies to vanish when a parent comment is deleted. The thread builder only keeps top-level comments that are not archived, so deleting a top-level comment removes its entire reply subtree.

A sixth bug prevents newly added mentions from triggering alerts. When a comment is edited to include a new handle, the system does not notify that person. The comment also retains its old mention list and fails to index the new wording for search.

The `updateComment` service method only persists the new body and timestamp. It never re-resolves mentions from the updated text, so `mentionedUserIds` stays stale. It also omits an edit event, which prevents fresh alerts and search reindexing. The fix requires re-scanning the new text for mentions on every edit, updating the stored user IDs, and emitting the appropriate event to trigger alerts and refresh search.

A seventh bug breaks the fifteen-minute edit window. The code checks `updatedAt` to decide if a comment is still editable, but that timestamp updates on every save. This means once a user edits a comment, they can keep editing indefinitely because the window never expires. The check should instead use `createdAt`, the original posting time.

Mention alerts should take precedence over comment alerts when a user receives both. For replies, the parent comment author must also be notified. The current comment.created event lacks parentId and parent author data, so the system needs to look up the parent comment to find its author.

Clarified the recipient hierarchy. Comment alerts go to the issue author, current assignee, and direct parent comment author for replies. Mention alerts target only the people named in the text. If a user appears in both groups, they receive only the mention alert. The comment author is excluded from both notification types.

Found a bug where replies to replies are missing from the thread view. The current listThread query only maps direct children, so deeper reply chains are not collected. The system needs to walk the full comment tree and gather all descendants under each root in posting order.

A recursive descendant collection algorithm will gather all replies under each root. Since the child list is already sorted by createdAt, chronological ordering is preserved automatically.

Clarified that thread replies must appear in flat chronological order, not depth-first tree traversal. The algorithm will collect every descendant comment under a root and sort them by createdAt.

content.thinking:
I found important UI bugs.

CommentThread hides deleted comments and their replies. Deleted parents disappear entirely, so replies under them vanish from the UI even if the repository returns them.

Deleted replies are also stripped out before they reach CommentItem. The component should preserve them as placeholders so replies remain anchored, but it currently removes them entirely.

The comment count also excludes deleted comments. Both the repository and UI need fixes to preserve deleted placeholders and keep replies anchored.

Search indexing is missing a comment.updated event. Only comment.created and comment.deleted are handled, so updated comments never reach the search index. Three fixes are under consideration: adding the event, emitting a reindex request, or calling the indexer directly from updateComment.

Checking page request schemas for max limits, activity service comment events, search tests, and member queries.

Checking whether members can be listed without pagination. The comment schema caps mentionedUserIds at 50, but this limit applies to client-provided input rather than resolved mentions. All resolved mentions will be stored regardless.

Only active members should be resolved for mentions. Invited and suspended members must be excluded. The current member query includes invited and suspended users unless status is filtered. Also verifying whether client-provided user IDs from other organizations are properly handled.

The author's own handle is excluded from mentions. Shared handles must resolve to multiple user IDs instead of a single one. Members with identical handles should appear in first-appearance order.

The spec does not define ordering for members sharing a handle. The current map overwrites entries, so all matching user IDs must be collected instead. Existing tests expect [ALICE, BOB] for "@alice @bob.smith". Member list order from the repository may be newest-first.

Case-insensitivity is already handled by lowercasing. The bug is in mention resolution, not highlighting: names appear highlighted in the text but are not listed as mentioned. Code spans are ignored by extractMentions, yet highlightMentions does not ignore them.

The 100-member limit and viewer skip are separate issues from the highlight function. The bug report confirms names are correctly highlighted in text but not recorded as mentions, so the resolution logic is the actual problem. Highlighting inside code spans will remain unchanged unless necessary.

The 100-member lookup limit is caused by a capped page size in listMembers. Members are ordered newest-first, so older active members beyond the cap are never found. A dedicated repository method that returns all active, non-archived members for an organization will bypass this cap.

Cursor-based pagination was considered but rejected as fragile. A dedicated `listActiveMembers(orgId)` repository method will return all active members without pagination limits.

Client-provided user IDs will be ignored. Only mentions resolved from the text will be recorded, since the spec requires exact text-based mentions.

Existing tests pass with empty client-provided IDs, so removing the union logic will not break them. The spec overrides the old server-wins behavior and requires recording only text-resolved mentions. On comment edits, only newly mentioned members should receive alerts; previously mentioned members must be skipped.

Author exclusion should happen after mention resolution, not inside the resolver. Filtering by userId alone would incorrectly include members who share the author's handle.

Reconsidering the author exclusion rule. The phrase "whose own handle is ignored" likely means the author's handle itself is excluded from mentions, not just their user ID. This would prevent members who share that handle from being mentioned as well.

The author exclusion rule is now interpreted as a self-mention guard. When the text contains the author's handle, only the author themselves is excluded from being recorded as mentioned. Members who share that same handle are still resolved and included.

No comment.updated event exists. Re-emitting comment.created would incorrectly notify watchers of a new comment. Adding a new event is too invasive. The best approach is to call notify() directly from the comment service for newly mentioned users with kind comment_mention.
I'll examine how issue updates trigger search reindexing to mirror that behavior for comments.

Reviewing the issue update pattern and checking search functionality.

The listThread bug causes reply-to-reply comments to appear in the total count but not in the thread. The UI also filters out deleted comments instead of showing them as placeholders. Need to fix both the thread display and the UI filtering.

Removing the `isLive` filter from CommentThread will let deleted replies render as placeholders. Deleted top-level comments must also stay visible even without replies, and the empty state should display those placeholders instead of "No comments yet".

The repository also filters out archived top-level comments. Deleted replies are only included when their parent is live; otherwise the node drops entirely. Nested replies are not attached to the top-level comment at all.

Deleted nested comments should appear as placeholders in the flattened descendant list. The UI already hides archived text, but the API may still return the body. The spec requires the comment to be marked as deleted and without its text.

The archive function should also clear the comment body to ensure deleted text is not leaked via the API. Need to verify whether archiveComment currently only applies an archive patch.

The existing test only verifies that `archivedAt` is set, not that the body is cleared. Clearing the body on archive will also remove the old text from the search index. This satisfies the requirement to keep deleted comments without their text while preserving the placeholder in the thread.

Clearing the body during archiving is safe because the database has no minimum length constraint, and the archive operation bypasses the standard update schema. Replies will not cascade delete; only the target comment gets archived. For reply-to-reply notifications, the author of the original comment being answered should be notified.

The comment.created event does not include a parentId. The notification handler will load the comment by ID to check for a parent and notify that author. A Set will collect unique watchers to prevent duplicate notifications.

The notification handler will load the parent comment to identify its author for reply-to-reply alerts. Mentioned users are filtered from the general watcher list to avoid duplicate notifications. The existing notify function already skips the actor and deduplicates recipients.

Mentioned users must be removed from the general comment recipient list before calling notify, since overlapping lists would trigger duplicate alerts. Edge cases are verified: parent authors and assignees are skipped by the actor filter, and Set deduplication prevents double notifications when roles overlap. The existing test for mentioned users aligns with this logic.

The edit window should use createdAt rather than updatedAt.

The edit window currently only blocks the comment author. Members and admins can edit any comment regardless of ownership, since the permission matrix grants comment:update to members and above. The spec says permission rules for editing other people's comments do not apply to those who are allowed to do so.

Viewers are rank 1 and cannot edit other people's comments, so the 15-minute window only applies to the comment author. Members and admins editing another user's comment bypass the window entirely. Platform staff can also edit via a staff bypass.

The edit window fix will use createdAt directly rather than the existing constant. For comment edits, updateComment must re-resolve mentions from the new body, persist the updated mentionedUserIds, and alert only users newly mentioned.

The search index updates on comment.

No `comment.updated` event exists. Adding one would require schema changes. Calling the search index directly from the comment service would create unwanted coupling.
